meta.title: HookShield — open-source, zero-trust webhook gateway
meta.description: Receive, verify, transform, encrypt and reliably deliver every webhook. Retries, alerts and a live debugger. Self-host free in one click or use HookShield Cloud.

hero.title: Webhooks that never get lost.
hero.subtitle: HookShield sits in front of your app: it checks every webhook at the edge, transforms it, encrypts it with AES-256-GCM and delivers it with retries, alerts and a live debugger.
hero.note: Free Cloud plan, no card. Self-hosted is free forever, with no plan limits.
hero.screenshotAlt: HookShield dashboard: requests, delivery rate, latency and the live feed of webhooks

pipeline.title: An edge pipeline in front of every endpoint
pipeline.subtitle: Senders get an answer in milliseconds. Everything else happens in the background, encrypted.

guard.title: Token guard
guard.body: Header token, HMAC signature or IP allow-list. Bad calls get a 401 before anything is stored.

transform.title: Transform
transform.body: Remove, add, rename and format fields and headers, with a live input → output preview.

encrypt.title: Encrypt
encrypt.body: Bodies and headers are encrypted with AES-256-GCM before they even reach the queue.

deliver.title: Deliver
deliver.body: Exponential backoff, configurable retries, Retry-After, dead-letter queue and one-click replay.

alert.title: Alert
alert.body: Slack, Telegram, email or webhook when a destination keeps failing, grouped so you are not spammed.

pipeline.latency: p99 {ms} ms to accept a webhook
pipeline.latencyNote: Measured at 200 requests/s on a 2 vCPU machine running everything.

features.title: Everything a webhook needs between the sender and your app

debugger.title: Debugger with a timeline
debugger.body: Every request with its latency per stage, the original and transformed payloads, the destination's response and every attempt.

replay.title: Replay and sandbox
replay.body: Replay any webhook, or send a test event through the whole pipeline from the dashboard or the CLI.

secrets.title: Secrets vault
secrets.body: Inject API keys into outbound headers with {{secrets.NAME}}. Encrypted, never shown again, never sent to the CLI.

retries.title: Retry policies
retries.body: Fixed, exponential or custom intervals per endpoint. Failed deliveries go to a dead-letter queue you can replay.

ssrf.title: SSRF protection
ssrf.body: Deliveries to private, loopback and cloud metadata addresses are refused on the IP actually dialled.

keyboard.title: Keyboard first
keyboard.body: ⌘K finds any endpoint, request, page or action. Dark by default, with a light theme one keystroke away.

languages.title: In your language
languages.body: The dashboard, emails and alerts are fully translated into English, Portuguese and Spanish.

api.title: API and API keys
api.body: Endpoints, logs, replays, transforms, secrets and alerts are all in the REST API (OpenAPI spec included), with scoped keys for CI and scripts.

screens.title: Built for debugging at 2 a.m.
screens.debugger: Request debugger: per-stage latency, payloads and every attempt
screens.transform: Transform editor with a live preview of what your app will receive
screens.endpoints: Endpoints with their URL, authentication and success rate

cli.title: Real webhooks on localhost
cli.body: hookshield listen forwards each webhook to your local app exactly as HookShield delivers it — body byte for byte, so Stripe and GitHub signatures still verify. No tunnel to configure.

selfHost.title: Your server, your keys, no limits
selfHost.body: The self-hosted edition is the same gateway and dashboard as Cloud, under the MIT license: no request quota, no plan limits, no license key. Your encryption key never leaves your server.
selfHost.composeNote: HTTPS by Caddy, one domain, backups included.
selfHost.oneClickNote: Each button deploys the all-in-one image with PostgreSQL and Redis. The encryption key is generated for you — back it up.

pricing.title: Free to start. Pay as you grow.
pricing.subtitle: HookShield Cloud runs, scales and backs up the gateway for you. Prices in USD; taxes are handled by Paddle, our merchant of record.
pricing.everything: Every feature, alert channel and the CLI

selfHosted.title: Self-hosted
selfHosted.body: Same gateway and dashboard, MIT licensed, no plan limits. You run it.

pricing.billingNote: Retries never count toward your requests: only webhooks you receive, replays and test events do.

security.title: Zero trust, all the way down

items.encryption: AES-256-GCM for every payload and header, stored secret and alert channel, with a random nonce per record
items.tokens: Endpoint tokens and API keys stored only as hashes; argon2id for passwords
items.ssrf: Outbound SSRF guard on the dialled IP, no redirects followed
items.sessions: HttpOnly sessions, CSRF checks, a Content-Security-Policy and login throttling per email and IP
items.audit: Security-reviewed before release; findings and known limitations are public in the security policy
items.open: Open source: read every line, report issues privately

free.q: Is the self-hosted edition really free?
free.a: Yes. It is MIT licensed and has no request quota, plan limits or license key. HookShield Cloud adds hosting, plans and billing on top of the same open-source core.

down.q: What happens when my app is down?
down.a: HookShield has already answered the sender, so nothing is lost. Deliveries are retried with backoff; after the last attempt the webhook goes to the dead-letter queue, you get an alert, and you can replay it from the dashboard.

guarantees.q: What delivery guarantee do I get?
guarantees.a: At-least-once. Every delivery carries an X-HookShield-Id header so your app can ignore duplicates. Ordering between webhooks is not guaranteed.

storage.a: Encrypted, for the retention of your plan (24 hours on Developer, 30 days on Pro, 90 days on Business), so you can inspect and replay them. Self-hosted installs choose their own retention.

providers.q: Does it work with Stripe, GitHub, Shopify…?
providers.a: With any sender that makes an HTTP request. HookShield keeps the body byte for byte, so the provider's signature can still be verified by your app.

latency.a: Accepting a webhook takes a few milliseconds (p99 under 20 ms in our benchmark); the transform, storage and delivery happen asynchronously. Workers scale horizontally.
